'''''Mie kocok''''' ({{lit|shaken noodle}}) is an [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian]] [[beef]] [[noodle soup]], a specialty of [[Bandung]] City, [[West Java]]. The dish consists of noodles served in rich beef consommé soup, {{lang|id|kikil}} (beef [[Tendon as food|tendon]] or slices of [[cow's trotters]]), [[bean sprout]]s and [[bakso]] (beef meatball), [[kaffir lime]] juice, and sprinkled with sliced fresh [[celery]], [[scallion]], and fried [[shallot]]. Some recipes might add beef [[tripe]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Mie Kocok Bandung | date=July 24, 2013 | url=http://www.au.timeout.com/sydney/restaurants/venues/5889/mie-kocok-bandung | publisher=Time Out Sydney | access-date=May 20, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521031523/http://www.au.timeout.com/sydney/restaurants/venues/5889/mie-kocok-bandung | archive-date=May 21, 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

In [[Indonesian language|Indonesian]] the term {{lang|id|kocok}} means "shake", and it refers to the method of softening and cooking the noodles by shaking the noodles placed in a handled porous tin container while being simmered in hot water.<ref>{{cite web| title=Mie Kocok, Noodle With Thick Beef Soup Plus Kikil From Bandung | date=Feb 4, 2013| url=http://inloveindonesia.com/mie-kocok-mie-dengan-kaldu-sapi-kental-plus-kikil-khas-bandung/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520220936/http://inloveindonesia.com/mie-kocok-mie-dengan-kaldu-sapi-kental-plus-kikil-khas-bandung/ | url-status=usurped | archive-date=May 20, 2014 | publisher=In Love Indonesia| access-date=May 20, 2014 }}</ref> The dish uses flat yellow noodles.

To add taste and spiciness {{lang|id|[[kecap manis]]}} (sweet soy sauce) and {{lang|id|[[sambal]]}} might be added. A similar but slightly different chicken-based noodle dish from the neighboring city of [[Cirebon]] is called {{lang|jv|[[mie koclok]]}}.
